name: Merlot
lede: Merlot is a very dark purplish red named for the red wine grape, recorded in the 2010 xkcd color survey and also known in our library as Claret Violet.

sections.title: A wine-grape name
sections.body:
Our Color Graph files Merlot, #730039, as a plant, animal, food or landscape name, after the red wine grape merlot, recorded in the xkcd survey of 2010 [1]. Our sources do not trace how long the color name has paired with the grape name before that survey; the origin beyond the general naming category is undocumented here [1]. The ISCC-NBS system classes the hue as deep purplish red, about 5.1 units from that block's center [1]. Its Munsell notation is 0.7R 2.3/9.8 and its LCH values are lightness 24, chroma 47, hue 1 degree, one of the darkest colors in our library [1]. The library also files this same swatch under the name Claret Violet, and its nearest common match is [[burgundy]], a related wine-dark red [2].

See [[burgundy]] and [[claret]] for the better-documented wine-red names this color sits beside.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has a color within CIEDE2000 4 of Merlot covering even 1% of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole: a color this dark and this saturated is hard for any museum photograph of an aged, varnished canvas to hold onto [3].
